items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: there was Lawrence Brown with the Duke Ellington Orchestra, he had just a gorgeous sound and a great sense of swing

ctx.x: Well, remember I always wanted to play the trumpet and in recent years I’m starting to play more and more cornet actually. But I try to approach the trumpet, or I try to approach the trombone more like a trumpet. And Louis is my big hero actually. If I had to pick one it would be Louis. And then I don’t know who the second one would be you

know, I mean there are so many guys I love, but Louis is number one. And I keep thinking about him and I keep thinking about playing as simply as I can. And this may be something that comes with age. I remember when I was 15 trying to do everything under the sun. And I was about 18 when I heard my first Charlie Parker record and — well no I can’t say that, I guess I was in high school — and I just didn’t get it. I really didn’t get it. And some students then in college, they said, “Hey Dan, I hear you’re…

the first half of your career you spend trying to sound like other guys and then the second half, if you’re smart, you spend it trying not to sound like those guys. You’re just trying to find your own voice.
